category: pay-per-file premium download service (no subscription, no account)

free_tier.stated: None. The pricing table lists up to 0.5 GB at USD 0.90, 0.5-1 GB at USD 0.99 and each extra GB above 1 at USD 0.33; no account is created and there is no monthly fee.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated: the price is computed per file from its size ('we check the file and price in real time')

retention.stated: not stated; the link is shown on-page and emailed

egress.terms: Each download is priced individually from a published size table: up to 0.5 GB at USD 0.90, 0.5-1 GB at USD 0.99 and each extra GB above 1 at USD 0.33.
egress.price_per_tb: not published as a rate; priced per file

interface_detail: Web form only; payment by Crypto (Cryptomus: USDT, BTC, ETH) or PayPal. No API is documented.
tooling: Browser only; no download-manager integration named.
chaining: It is the only service here that turns a single file into a known cash price before download, which makes it the fallback when a subscription's host list fails and one file must still arrive.

limits.value: pay per byte, priced per file; no free allowance

limits_note: 'Works with 155+ hosts'; no monthly cap, no concurrency figure, no per-host limits published.
binding_note: Money is the counter: every byte is bought, so at 1 TiB a month the constraint is the invoice rather than a rate or a shaping rule. The site publishes no per-GB rate, so the invoice cannot be predicted without submitting a file.

identity_cost.detail: 'no signup' and 'no accounts to create'; the download link is emailed, so an email address is optional rather than required, and payment is by crypto or PayPal.

reliability_note: Pay-per-file removes subscription risk but leaves balance risk: a top-up bonus encourages prepaying into a wallet held by an operator with no status page.
confidence_note: The pay-per-file model, the host count, the top-up bonuses and the payment rails are vendor-stated and read today. The actual price of any file was not measured because that requires submitting a link and a payment.

evidence.proved: 'No subscriptions - you pay per file', 'Works with 155+ hosts', the top-up bonuses (+10/+15/+20%), Cryptomus and PayPal rails, 'no signup'
no free tier: no account to create and no monthly fee
evidence.quote: No spammy ads, no account to create, no monthly fee.

evidence.proved: no signup; an email address is the only identity detail
evidence.quote: Anonymous checkout: we only need the email your link is sent to.

evidence.proved: the vendor now publishes a per-file size/price table instead of a flat per-file price
the vendor states there is no account or monthly fee; pricing detail comes from the size table
evidence.quote: No spammy ads, no account to create, no monthly fee.

notes: The absence of a published per-GB rate is the finding: the same service sells files at a price it computes at submission time, so a client cannot budget a terabyte month without sampling. Useful as a one-file fallback, not as a base.
